subject.title: Feature Request: Session rotation/archive lifecycle event for cron job triggers

question: Should session archive/rotation automation be supported through the existing plugin `session_end` lifecycle plus a narrow SDK seam, or should OpenClaw add a first-class core Cron event schedule for session archive/rotation?
rationale: The code already has adjacent plugin lifecycle and Cron primitives, but the permanent shape affects public Cron config, plugin SDK boundaries, and security-sensitive archived-session metadata.

options.title: Use plugin lifecycle plus narrow SDK seam
options.body: Bless `session_end` as the session-boundary signal and add only the smallest SDK scheduling or event-dispatch capability external plugins need to run this workflow safely.

options.title: Add core Cron lifecycle schedules
options.body: Define `schedule.kind: event` for session archive/rotation in the Gateway protocol with scoped metadata, permissions, persistence, trace output, docs, and tests.

options.title: Route to plugin workflow only
options.body: If maintainers decide current plugin hooks are sufficient, document the supported plugin pattern and leave workflow packaging to ClawHub or external plugin repos.

recommendation.title: Use plugin lifecycle plus narrow SDK seam
recommendation.body: Bless `session_end` as the session-boundary signal and add only the smallest SDK scheduling or event-dispatch capability external plugins need to run this workflow safely.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision sits at the hook/plugin API boundary where the strongest recent history and related maintainer direction point.
